questions.question: Use the particle model to explain why a brass ball that fits through a ring at room temperature does not fit when heated. State what happens to the size of the particles, the mass and the density.
questions.expected_answer: When the ball is heated its particles gain energy and vibrate more vigorously about their positions, pushing further apart on average, so the ball's volume increases and it no longer fits through the ring. The particles themselves do not change size; only the spaces between them increase. The number of particles is unchanged, so the mass stays the same; since the same mass occupies a larger volume, the density decreases. When it cools the particles move closer together, it contracts and fits again.

questions.question: Arrange solids, liquids and gases in order of how much they expand for the same temperature rise, explain the order, and describe what is unusual about water between 0 °C and 4 °C.
questions.expected_answer: Solid expands least, then liquid, then gas expands most. The order is due to the strength of forces between particles: strongest in solids, which resist being pushed apart; weaker in liquids; very weak in gases, so gas particles spread out most easily. Water is unusual: when warmed from 0 °C to 4 °C it contracts instead of expanding, so it is densest at about 4 °C; above 4 °C it expands normally.

questions.question: Give two problems caused by expansion and how each is solved, and explain how a bimetallic strip switches off an electric iron.
questions.expected_answer: Railway lines: rails expand in summer and could buckle, so gaps are left between rail lengths (or rails are anchored as stressed welded rail). Bridges: decks expand and contract, so expansion joints and rollers or sliding bearings are fitted. Power lines contract in winter and could snap, so they are hung with sag. A bimetallic strip is two metals (e.g. brass and steel) joined together; when heated, brass expands more than steel so the strip bends. In an iron, the strip carries a contact in the circuit; as the iron heats up the strip bends away and breaks the contact, switching off the heating element; as it cools it straightens and switches it on again.
